feature: A full-screen Retina recording keeps up while it plays
summary: Playing a 3456x2234 recording now shows the frame under the playhead every time. Before, 17 of 24 looks showed a frame up to 16 frames (half a second) old, so the picture stuck and jumped.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Press Space and watch the first second: the coloured line should sweep smoothly.
Press Space to pause, then Space again to play on.
While it plays, drag the playhead back to the start and let go.
Open a recording with cuts in it and play across a cut.
Press J, then L twice, to play backwards and at double speed.

evaluate: Does the full-screen recording move as smoothly as a small one from the first second?
When you pause, is the paused frame as sharp and the same colours as it was before this change?
After a scrub while playing, does the picture pick up straight away from where you let go?
Does playing across a cut ever show a frame from before the cut for a moment?
rough: Before and after, same walk, same machine: before 17, 21 and 19 of 24 looks late, by up to 16 or 18 frames; after 0 of 24 in four runs in a row, and 0 of 24 with ten cores busy with other work.
Playing backwards (J) still reads frame by frame, the old slow way, so a full-screen recording played backwards can still lag. No mock covers backward playback, and nobody has reported it.

A cut that jumps to another part of the same recording, or a dissolve between two parts of one recording, reads the far side frame by frame. The editing-session walk plays across its cuts and dissolve with every frame in time, but a very short piece of a full-screen recording could still be a frame or two late.

The picture attached is the real window after playing to the end. The walk's 'while playing' snapshot is taken after its own check has already played to 3.0s of a 3.6s file, so it lands at the end. No mock covers this surface: nothing on screen changed, only how quickly frames arrive.
